0: 32 CHATTOOGA COUNTY FREESTANDING SIGN REGULATIONS ORDINANCE CHAPTERl. GENERALLY
1: This ordinance is enacted for the purpose of regulating the placement of signs and billboards within Chattooga County, Georgia.
2:
A. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this ordinance shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clemly indicates a different meaning: 1. Area of sign: The area within a continuous perimeter enclosing the limits of writing, representation, emblem, or any figure of similar character together with any frame, other material, open space, or color forming an integral part of the display or used to differentiate such writing, representation, emblem or any figure of similar character from the background against which it is placed. The sign area of painted or affixed wall signs when composed of letters only is the sum of the areas of the smallest contiguous rectangles each capable of containing one such letter. For double-faced signs, only the largest display face shall be measured in computing the sign area. 2. 'Height of sign: The distru1ce in vertical feet from the ground to the highest point of the sign face. 3. Monument sign: Any ground sign which has a brick or stone base and frame within which advertising panels are contained at the base and sides. 4. Nonconforming sign: Any sign which lawfully e;~isted on the effective date of this ordinance but which does not conform to the provisions of this ordinance. All nonconforming signs have five (5) years from date of this ordinance to be brought into conformity or face condemnation. 5. Sign: A lettered, numbered, symbolic, pictorial, or illuminated visual display, device, flag, banner, or communication designated or used for the purpose of identifying, announcing, directing, informing, or bringing to the attention of others the subject thereon, that is visible from the public right-of-way and which is permanently affixed and wholly independent of a building for support (i.e., freestanding). 6. Sign face: That part of a sign that is or can be used for advertising purposes.

- 7. Billboard: Any sign in excess ofone hundred and fifty (150) square feet which lawfully existed on the effective date of this ordinance which sign is freestanding and erected on single post or poles.
3: The provisions of this ordinance shall apply to all signs erected within the unincorporated area of Chattooga County, Georgia, which are wholly independent of a building for suppmi and are visible from a public right-of"way and are in excess of eighty-five (85) square feet in total size and arc in the same location for a period in excess of six mdnlhs.
4: It shall be unlawful for any person to post, display, substantially change, or erect a sign regulated by this ordinance in the County without first baving obtained a building pennit. The applicant fot a building permit shall submit application materials as specified by the Building Inspector.

Applications for pem1its for signs shall be filed by the sign owner or his agent in the office of the Building fospector upon forms furnished by said office. Appropriate fees to cover the cost of permit application shall be establislied by Chattooga County. The application shall describe and set forth the following: A. A description of the type and purpose of the sign as defined in this ordinance. B. A drawing of the sign which shows the height of the sign, the area of the face of the sign, and the structural supports of the sign. · C. The street address oflhe property upon which subject sign is to be located and the proposed location of subject sign on subject property. D. A survey or tax plat of the property on which the sign will be located which shows where thereon the sign will be located and the distance from the property lines and the paved street right-of-way. E. The name(s) and address(es) of the owner(s) of the real property upon which the subject sign is to be located, and consent of the owner, or his agent, granting permission for the placement or maintenance of subject sign, which may include a copy of the lease or other document from the owner of the sign which authorized the erection thereof F. The name, address, phone number and business registration number (if required) of the sign contractor. 33

34 the Building Inspector shall be authorized to issue permits for signs in accordance with the provisions of this ordinance. All permit applications pursuant to this ordinance shall be processed within ten (10) business days of the County's actual receipt of a complete permit application and a permit fee.
6: All signs regulated by this ordinance shall be maintained by the property owner in good co11ditio11 so as to present a neat and orderly appearance or after thirty (30) days notice may be removed by the Building Inspector or other County authorities.
7: The maximum height of any sign regulated by this article shall be twenty (20) feet.
8: The maximum size of any sign face shall not exceed one hundred fifty (150) square feet.
9: Back to back or v-formation signs are allowed but side"to-side or top-and-bottom signs are prohibited.
10: No sign regulated by this ordinance shall be placed or erected closer than thirty (30) feet of a city, county, state or federal road right-of-way or closer than thirty-five (35) feet from the rightof-way line intersection point measured at any angle,
11:
The Commissioner shall have authority to authorize upon application in specific cases such variance from the terms of this ordinance as will not be contrary to the public interest, when due to special conditions a literal enforcement of the provisions of these sign regulations will, in an individual case, result in unusual hardship, so the spirit of the sign regulations shall be observed, public safety and welfare secured, and substantial justice done. Applications for variances shall be made to the Building Inspector on forms provided by that office and shall be accompanied by a fee for said application as may be established by resolution of the Commissioner from time to time and other application materials specified by the Building Inspector as may be needed to ensure compliance with this ordinance and evaluate the requested variance.

A. Criteria for approval of sign variances: A variance may be granted upon application in an individual case of unusual hardship upon a finding by the Commissioner that all of the following conditions exist: l. There exist extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the property in question resulting from its size, shape, or toj)ography which are not applicable to other lands or structures in the area. • 2. A literal interpretation of the provisions of this ordinance would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other similar properties. 3. Granting the variance requested will not confer upon the property of the applicant any significant privileges which are denied to other similar properties. 4. the requested variance will be in hannony with the purpose and intent of these regulations and will not be injurious to the neighborhood or to the general welfare. 5. the special circumstances are not the result of actions of the applicant. 6. The variance is not a request to permit a type of sign which otherwise is prohibited by this otdinance. 7. the mere existence of a nonconforming sign or advertising device shall not constitute a valid reason to grant a variance. · 8. Variances granted shall be reviewed every two (2) years by the Building Inspector and renewed or removed pending his determination.

All sign locations shall be no less than 2,500 feet apart, measuring from the two closest points, on the same side of the road from another sign on any roadway of unincorporated Chattooga County including state highways. B. Signs shall not be erected at any location having principal frontage on any street v.rithin 1,000 feet of any designated parkway or scenic byway.
13: There shall be no roof mounted signs. 35
14: No additional billboard signs may be erected in Chattooga County, Georgia. All billboards signs shall be maintained in a neat and orderly appearance and if not, upon thirty (30) days notice to correct said appearance may be removed by the Building Inspector or other County Authority.
15: All illuminated signs shall use base-mounted lights and shall be activated by photoelectric cells. Such lights shall be directed only on the sign face arid shall be effectively shielded so as to prevent beams or rays of light from being directed into any portion of the roadway. The illumination of any sign within l 00 feet of any residential use shall be defused or designed to prevent direct fays oflight from shining into those adjoining uses. Additional lighting, including but not limited to animation or ru1111ing lights, shall be prohibited. Metal, plastic faceted, or disc material sometimes referred to as solaray or other material that may appear to provide the effect of motion shall be prohibited, No revolving or rotating beam of light that resembles or simulates any ernetgency light device shall be permitted as part of any sign. Flashing devices shall not be permitted upon a sign; however, illuminated signs that indicate customary public information such as time, date, tempei-ature or other similar information shall be permitted.
16: Extensions or extrusions beyond the face of the sign, excluding-aprons; shall be prohibited.
17: No sign shall be placed in or obstruct the view of an area that has historic interest.
